en.title: Most Frequent Substring with Limited Distinct Characters
en.description:
Among contiguous substrings with length in [minLength,maxLength] and a number of distinct characters ≤maxUnique, find the maximum number of occurrences of the same text; overlapping occurrences are allowed. Return 0 if no substring qualifies.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: This site's JSON input: [s,minLength,maxLength,maxUnique], which may contain escaped whitespace or Unicode; lengths are counted in Unicode characters. The original text gives no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤|s|≤100000, 1≤minLength≤maxLength≤|s|, and 1≤maxUnique≤100000.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3; 2; 2. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Only the shortest length L needs to be considered: the length-L prefix of any longer substring occurs at least as often and has no more distinct characters. Mark the qualifying length-L windows with a sliding window, use a suffix automaton to count the occurrences of each substring exactly, and filter the states that represent length L.
